'''Paul Howard Frampton''' is an English theoretical physicist who works in [[Phenomenology (physics)|particle theory]] and cosmology. From 1996 until 2014, he was the Louis D. Rubin, Jr. [[Distinguished Professor]] of physics and astronomy at the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]]. After a well-publicised hiatus involving being victimised by a romance scam, convicted of drug smuggling in Argentina, and fired by UNC (in which he won a lawsuit for wrongful termination), he later became affiliated with the Department of Mathematics and Physics of the [[University of Salento]], in Italy.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.paulframpton.org/about/|title=Paul Frampton Home Page – Paul Frampton}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Paul-Frampton|title=Researchgate references Paul Frampton, Univ. of Salento}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web| title=Tornabene’s Collocation in the Career 2017,2018 & 2019 (1996‐2019) rankings considering the C‐Indicator | url=https://www.unisalento.it/documents/20152/868015/Tornabene+Collocation+in+the+100000+Top+Scientists+List+2020.pdf/0d4facbd-baa7-8bb2-71d1-4159c36eb30c?version=1.0&download=true | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420195419/https://www.unisalento.it/documents/20152/868015/Tornabene+Collocation+in+the+100000+Top+Scientists+List+2020.pdf/0d4facbd-baa7-8bb2-71d1-4159c36eb30c?version=1.0&download=true | archive-date=2024-04-20}}</ref>

==Early life==
{{unreferencedsect|date=September 2026}}
Born in [[Kidderminster]], England, Frampton attended [[King Charles I School]] from 1954 to 1962 and then [[Brasenose College, Oxford]] from 1962 to 1968. He received the degrees of BA ([[British undergraduate degree classification#Variations in classification|double first]]) in 1965, MA, DPhil in 1968 and DSc in 1984, all from the [[University of Oxford]].

==Career==
He is a Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science (1990) and the American Physical Society (1981). In 1987, he was the project director for siting the [[Superconducting Supercollider]], in [[North Carolina]]. A [[Festschrift]] was published for his 60th birthday in 2003.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cgc.physics.miami.edu/2003CGC.html|title=La Belle Epoque of High Energy Physics and Cosmology|last=Curtright|first=T.|author2=Mintz, S.|year=2004|publisher=World Scientific Publishing Company.|author3=Perlmutter, A.|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141209210659/https://cgc.physics.miami.edu/2003CGC.html|archive-date=9 December 2014}}</ref>

His [[DPhil]] thesis analysed the relationship between [[current algebra]] and [[superconvergence]] [[Sum rule in quantum mechanics|sum rules]], and contained a 1967 sum rule. In 1970, he analysed the absence of [[Ghost (physics)|ghosts]] in the [[dual resonance model]].

Three examples of his model building are the [[chiral color]] model, in 1987, which predicts [[axigluon]]s; the [[331 model]], in 1992, which can explain the number of quark-lepton generations, and predicts [[bilepton]]s; and his proposal, in 1995, of the [[binary tetrahedral group]] as a [[Flavour (particle physics)|flavor]] symmetry. All three serve as targets of opportunity for the [[Large Hadron Collider]] (LHC). In 2002, he built a model relating matter–antimatter asymmetry in the early universe to measurements possible on Earth. In 2015, he showed that the 331-model predicts long-lived quarks accessible to Run 2 of the LHC.
	
In formal directions, three examples are that he calculated, in 1976, the rate of [[vacuum decay]] in [[quantum field theory]]; in 1982, he analysed ten-dimensional [[gauge field theory]], and its hexagon anomaly, precursor to the [[first superstring revolution]]; and in 1988, he constructed the [[Lagrangian (field theory)|Lagrangian]] which describes the dynamics of the [[p-adic]] string.

For cosmology, two examples are, in 2007, he built a [[cyclic model]], which can solve a 75-year-old [[entropy]] problem; and in 2010, he discussed how [[dark energy]] may be better understood by studying [[temperature]] and entropy. In 2015, he demonstrated how cyclic entropy can lead to
flat geometry without an inflationary era and estimated the time until contraction to be close to one hundred times the present age of the universe. In 2015, he also proposed a novel theory of [[dark matter]], where the dark matter constituents are [[primordial black hole]]s with many solar masses.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Frampton |first1=Paul H. |last2=Kawasaki |first2=Masahiro |last3=Takahashi |first3=Fuminobu |last4=Yanagida |first4=Tsutomu T. |title=Primordial Black Holes as All Dark Matter |journal=Journal of Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics |date=22 April 2010 |volume=2010 |issue=4 |page=023 |doi=10.1088/1475-7516/2010/04/023 |arxiv=1001.2308 |bibcode=2010JCAP...04..023F |s2cid=119256778 }}</ref>

In 2022, he published the idea that the accelerated cosmologicial expansion is caused by Coulomb repulsion between
like-sign electrically-charged Primordial Extremely Massive
Black Holes (PEMBHs).<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Frampton |first1=Paul H.|title=Electromagnetic Accelerating Universe |journal=Physics Letters B |volume=835 |article-number=137480 |year=2022|doi=10.1016/j.physletb.2022.137480 |arxiv=2210.10632 |bibcode=2022PhLB..83537480F |s2cid=252891805 }}</ref>

===Drug smuggling conviction===
In January 2012, Frampton was arrested at a Buenos Aires airport after checking in a bag containing two kilograms of cocaine hidden in the lining. That November, Frampton was convicted of [[drug smuggling]] in Argentina and was sentenced to four years and eight months in detention.<ref name='PhysicsWorld'>{{cite web | url = http://physicsworld.com/cws/article/news/2012/nov/22/paul-frampton-hit-by-56-month-drugs-sentence | title = Paul Frampton hit by 56-month drugs sentence | access-date = 2013-04-02 | last = Banks | first = Michael | date = 22 Nov 2012 | work = [[Physics World]] | publisher = [[Institute of Physics]]}}</ref> He said that he was a victim of a [[romance scam]], and that he was tricked into [[Mule (smuggling)|transporting]] the suitcase.<ref name="NYT">{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2013/03/10/magazine/the-professor-the-bikini-model-and-the-suitcase-full-of-trouble.html?pagewanted=all&_r=0|title=The Professor, the Bikini Model and the Suitcase Full of Trouble|last=Swann|first=Maxine|author-link=Maxine Swann|date=8 March 2013|work=New York Times|access-date=18 March 2013}}</ref> While in prison, Frampton was diagnosed with [[schizoid personality disorder]] by a [[forensic psychologist]] hired by his legal team, a condition that Frampton says makes him gullible and more susceptible to such a scam.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Price|first1=Jay|date=7 June 2012|title=Professor accused of smuggling drugs says he has personality disorder|work=[[Standard-Examiner]]|url=https://www.standard.net/uncategorized/2012/jun/07/professor-accused-of-smuggling-drugs-says-he-has-personality-disorder/|access-date=1 September 2021}}</ref>

Soon after his arrest, his pay was stopped and he was placed on personal leave; the move was widely criticised by the academic community.<ref name="McClatchy">{{cite web|last=Price|first=Jay|date=23 October 2012|title=UNC professor Frampton asks for raise from Argentina jail|url=http://www.mcclatchydc.com/news/crime/article24739111.html|access-date=8 May 2017|publisher=[[McClatchy]] D.C.}}</ref><ref name="NO15"/> He was fired from his UNC post in 2014. On 16 June 2015, an appeals court in North Carolina unanimously ruled that his university violated its own policies by placing Frampton on unpaid leave while he awaited trial, and ordered the university to restore Frampton's back salary and benefits.<ref name="NO15">{{cite news|url=http://www.newsobserver.com/news/local/education/article24607696.html|last=Blythe|first=Anne|title=UNC Physics Professor jailed in Argentina wins back pay|date=16 June 2015|work=[[Raleigh News & Observer]]|access-date=25 June 2015}}</ref> Frampton's account of these events was published in 2014.<ref name=":0">{{cite book | last = Frampton| first = Paul| title = Tricked!: The story of an internet scam| year = 2014| asin = B00RBVDAD0 }}</ref>

Under Argentine law, a foreign national can be released from prison and deported after serving half of his or her sentence. Frampton was granted such release and returned to England in 2015, agreeing never to return to Argentina.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Blythe|first1=Anne|date=16 June 2015|title=UNC physics professor jailed in Argentina wins back pay|work=[[The News & Observer]]|url=https://www.newsobserver.com/news/local/education/article24607696.html|access-date=28 March 2021}}</ref>

=== Subsequent work ===
Since his return to England, Frampton has continued to author physics papers. These include ''A new direction for dark matter research: intermediate-mass compact halo objects'' (2016),<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Chapline |first1=George F. |last2=Frampton |first2=Paul H. |title=A new direction for dark matter research: intermediate-mass compact halo objects |journal=Journal of Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics |date=21 November 2016 |volume=2016 |issue=11 |page=042 |doi=10.1088/1475-7516/2016/11/042 |arxiv=1608.04297 |bibcode=2016JCAP...11..042C |s2cid=119298498 }}</ref> ''Exploring scalar and vector bileptons at the LHC in a 331 model'' (2018),<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Corcella |first1=Gennaro |last2=Corianò |first2=Claudio |last3=Costantini |first3=Antonio |last4=Frampton |first4=Paul H. |title=Exploring scalar and vector bileptons at the LHC in a 331 model |journal=Physics Letters B |date=October 2018 |volume=785 |pages=73–83 |doi=10.1016/j.physletb.2018.08.015 |arxiv=1806.04536 |bibcode=2018PhLB..785...73C |s2cid=119504001 }}</ref> and ''Electromagnetic accelerating universe'' (2022).<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Frampton |first1=Paul H. |title=Electromagnetic accelerating universe |journal=Physics Letters B |date=December 2022 |volume=835 |article-number=137480 |doi=10.1016/j.physletb.2022.137480 |arxiv=2210.10632 |bibcode=2022PhLB..83537480F |s2cid=252891805 }}</ref>

In 2023, he expanded the explanation of this novel cosmological model and showed the internal consistency when
there is no dark energy but only charged dark matter.<ref>
{{Cite journal|title=A Model of Dark Matter and Energy| first1=Paul H.|last1=Frampton|journal=Modern Physics Letters A|volume=38 |page=2350032 |year=2023| issue=5| doi=10.1142/S0217732323500323| arxiv=2301.10719| bibcode=2023MPLA...3850032F| s2cid=256231073}}</ref>

==Publications==
Frampton's first publication was ''Chirality Commutator and Vector Mesons'', in 1967. He has published more than 500 articles on particle theory and cosmology.{{cn|date=July 2024}} He is the author of a book<ref>{{cite book
 | last = Frampton
 | first = P.H.
 | title = Dual Resonance Models
 | publisher = Frontiers in Physics, W. A. Benjamin
 | year = 1974
 | isbn = 978-0-8053-2581-2
}}</ref> on [[string theory]], in 1974 (2nd edition, 1986), when it was still named the dual resonance model. In 1986, he published a book<ref>{{cite book
 | last = Frampton
 | first = P.H.
 | title = Gauge field theories
 | publisher = Frontiers in Physics, Addison-Wesley
 | year = 1986
 | isbn = 978-0-471-34783-5
}}</ref> on [[quantum field theory]] (2nd edition 2000, 3rd edition 2008). 
A book<ref>{{cite book
 | last = Frampton
 | first = P.H.
 | title = Did Time Begin? Will Time End?: Maybe the Big Bang never occurred
 | publisher = World Scientific Publishing Company
 | year = 2009
 | isbn = 978-981-4280-58-7
}}</ref> on cyclic [[cosmology]], for the general public, was published in 2009. A book on the history of particle theory was published in 2020.<ref>{{cite book
 |author = P.H. Frampton, J.E.Kim
 |year = 2020
 |title = History of Particle Theory
 |publisher = [[World Scientific Publishing Company]]
 |isbn = 978-981-12-2465-2
 }}</ref>
